plugins.name: camera-hw-accel
plugins.title: Camera HW Accel
plugins.description:
Tap into the SoC's video pipeline instead of CPU-encoding every frame. MJPEG over HTTP at /webcam, WebRTC at /webrtc; works on any browser, smooth 30fps even with two cameras attached.

To have these auto-registered as cameras in Fluidd and Mainsail (so you don't have to add them by hand under Settings → Cameras), also install b3d://bespok3d-org/webcam-builtin for the built-in MIPI camera and b3d://bespok3d-org/webcam-usb for the external USB camera.
plugins.tagline: HW-accelerated MJPEG and WebRTC streaming for MIPI & USB cameras.

config.label: WebRTC stream
config.hint: On by default: the Fluidd/Mainsail camera tile is registered for the WebRTC stream. Turning it off saves memory, but ONLY do so if your camera is set to the MJPEG stream, otherwise the tile goes blank.

config.label: Built-in camera resolution
config.hint: Capture resolution for the built-in (MIPI) camera. 720p uses less memory and CPU, handy on low-RAM boards. The external USB camera always uses its own native resolution.

config.label: Recycle WebRTC viewers after (minutes, 0 = off)
config.hint: 0 (recommended): a camera stays connected as long as you watch it. Set a number of minutes to periodically recycle each WebRTC viewer connection as a memory-safety backstop on a very constrained board; the tile reconnects on its own within a couple of seconds, so it no longer freezes. Dead or abandoned viewers are always cleaned up regardless of this setting.

plugins.name: fluidd
plugins.title: Fluidd
plugins.description: Swaps SM's outdated Fluidd for the current upstream release. You get input-shaper graphs, integrated config/G-code editors, tool-colour preview, modern mesh viz. Uninstall reverts to the SM-shipped copy automatically via overlayfs; no nginx config touched.
plugins.tagline: Modern Fluidd v1.37.0: replaces the stock SM build.

config.label: Fluidd port
config.hint: Auto-assigned. Make Fluidd primary to serve it on port 80.

plugins.name: mainsail
plugins.title: Mainsail
plugins.description: Installs Mainsail v2.17.0 as a second web frontend. Runs on port 81 by default so Fluidd stays on port 80. Set port 80 to make Mainsail primary; Fluidd shifts to 81 automatically.
plugins.tagline: Mainsail web interface alongside Fluidd, on your chosen port.

config.label: Mainsail port
config.hint: Auto-assigned. Make Mainsail primary to serve it on port 80.

plugins.name: moonraker-auth
plugins.title: Moonraker Login
plugins.description: Controls Moonraker's force_logins setting. When on, the web UI requires a login before any control; when off, local clients connect without logging in. Toggle the setting below before installing.
plugins.tagline: Require a login for the web UI, or allow open access.

config.label: Require login
config.hint: On: the web UI asks for a login before any control. Off: local clients connect without logging in.

plugins.name: octoeverywhere
plugins.title: OctoEverywhere
plugins.description: Free, secure remote access to your printer from anywhere, plus AI failure detection and remote notifications, via the OctoEverywhere cloud. This runs the official OctoEverywhere companion agent (a Moonraker companion) in its own isolated Python virtual environment; the app code and all its dependencies are baked into the package and installed offline, so the printer never runs pip or git. On first start the service logs a one-time link URL: open it to connect the printer to your OctoEverywhere account. OctoEverywhere is an external cloud service (free tier available); this plugin only runs the agent. Verified on a physical printer.
plugins.tagline: Free remote access + AI failure detection via the OctoEverywhere cloud.

plugins.name: panda-breath
plugins.title: Panda Breath
plugins.description: Drives a BIQU Panda Breath chamber-heating device as a standard Klipper heater. Adds a Klipper extra (panda_breath.py) that talks to the Panda Breath over its OEM WebSocket protocol, plus a [heater_generic] so you control chamber heat from the web UI and slicer like any other heater. Point it at your Panda Breath's host. The Panda Breath hardware is separate. Experimental: not yet verified on a physical device.
plugins.tagline: Chamber heating with a BIQU Panda Breath, as a Klipper heater.

config.label: Panda Breath host
config.hint: Hostname or IP of the Panda Breath. If .local does not resolve, use the IP.

plugins.name: remote-screen
plugins.title: Remote Screen
plugins.description:
Mirror the printer's on-device touchscreen to a browser. Low-overhead framebuffer capture, no UI changes on the device side.

To have the screen appear as a tile in Fluidd and Mainsail (alongside your cameras, no manual setup under Settings → Cameras), also install b3d://bespok3d-org/webcam-screen; registers the mirror as a Moonraker [webcam] iframe entry sized for the U1's 480:320 display.
plugins.tagline: Stream your printer's framebuffer as MJPEG.

plugins.name: rfid-ntag
plugins.title: RFID Spool Reader
plugins.description: USB RFID reader picks up OpenSpool-encoded NTAG215 cards. Writes the current spool's metadata to rfid_data.json on every card event so the rest of the stack just knows.
plugins.tagline: NTAG215/OpenSpool RFID: your filament knows what it is.

plugins.name: spoolman
plugins.title: Spoolman Bridge
plugins.description: Reads rfid_data.json at startup and on every card change, syncs the active spool to your Spoolman server. Length used per print is logged automatically.
plugins.tagline: Zero-config Spoolman: active spool always tracked.

macros.name: SET_ACTIVE_SPOOL
macros.description: Set the selected tool as the active spool.

macros.name: CLEAR_ALL_SPOOLS
macros.description: Clear the selected spool for every tool.

macros.name: DETECT_SPOOLS
macros.description: Re-detect the loaded spools. A handy reset when spool state looks wrong.

macros.name: DUMP_SPOOLS
macros.description: Print what the bridge knows about the loaded spools.

macros.name: READ_FILAMENT_ID
macros.description: Read the selected lane's spool tag, if any.

macros.name: GET_FILAMENT_ID
macros.description: Print the currently read tag for the selected lane.

macros.name: SH_CONFIG
macros.description: Change mode and logging at runtime, no restart.

macros.name: SH_DEBUG
macros.description: Print the current configuration; with a SKU, show the spool it would track.

config.label: Spoolman server address
config.hint: Host or host:port of your Spoolman instance.

config.label: Selection mode
config.hint: auto: RFID is the source of truth, falls back to the manual spool. manual: the manual selection drives, tags are the fallback.

config.label: Log level
config.hint: How chatty the logs are, from least to most.

plugins.name: timelapse
plugins.title: Timelapse
plugins.description: Adds a minimal Moonraker timelapse component and enables it, so the Timelapse menu shows up in Fluidd and Mainsail. Ships its own component, so it works on stock firmware where Moonraker has none.
plugins.tagline: Enable the Timelapse menu in Fluidd & Mainsail.
